{{Short description|American statistician}}

''For the American musician, see [[Wayne Nelson]].''

'''Wayne Nelson''' is an American statistician. His main contributions to the reliability theory are the [[Nelson–Aalen estimator|Nelson-Aalen Estimator]] for lifetime data, various statistical procedures for [[accelerated life testing]] and both: nonparametric and parametric procedures for [[recurrent data analysis]].

== Early life and education ==
Nelson was born in Chicago in 1936. He studied Physics at [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]] and graduated with a Bachelor of Science in 1958. Nelson obtained a Master of Science in Physics from the [[University of Illinois]] in 1959, then a Ph.D. in statistics from the same university in 1965.<ref name="GNE">{{cite web |url= http://www.gnedenko.net/Personalities/Nelson/Nelson_Wayne.htm|title= Wayne Nelson Biography}}</ref>

== Career ==

Nelson was employed from 1965 to 1989 at General Electric R&D.<ref name="Bio">{{cite web |url= https://accendoreliability.com/podcast/dtk/dtk-wayne-nelson-author/|title= Wayne Nelson Interview|last= Rodgers|first= Tim|date= January 2017}}</ref> He was also an adjunct professor teaching graduate courses on applications of statistics at [[Union College]] and [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]].<ref name="GNE" /> Currently, Nelson works as a private consultant and legal expert witness in statistical analysis and modeling of data in many industries; including automotive, aviation, electric power, electronics, materials, medical devices, microelectronics, military hardware, nuclear power, railroad, software, and transportation.<ref name="Bio" />

== Work ==
His research work focuses on collecting and analyzing reliability data, laboratory tests, accelerated tests, quality control, measurement error analysis, planned experiments, sampling, and data analysis. 
Nelson worked with [[Odd Aalen]] on constructing the [[Nelson-Aalen estimator|Nelson Aalen estimator]].,<ref name="hp">{{cite journal |last1=Nelson |first1=W. |title=Hazard plotting for incomplete failure data. |journal=Journal of Quality Technology |date=1969 |volume=1 |pages=27–52 |doi=10.1080/00224065.1969.11980344}}</ref><ref name="theory">{{cite journal |last1=Nelson |first1=W. |title=Theory and applications of hazard plotting for censored failure data |journal=Technometrics |date=1972 |volume=14 |issue=4 |pages=945–965 |doi=10.1080/00401706.1972.10488991}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Aalen |first1=Odd |title=Nonparametric inference for a family of counting processes|journal=Annals of Statistics |date=1978 |volume=6 |issue=4 |pages=701–726 |jstor=2958850 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/download/pdf_1/euclid.aos/1176344247 |doi=10.1214/aos/1176344247|doi-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref> a non-parametric approximation of the cumulative hazard function that can account for both failure and censored data. He also developed a method to estimate [[Weibull distribution]] (with few or no failures) for products with [[Continuous design|evolutionary design]] (same [[shape parameter]] β).<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Nelson|first1= Wayne|date= 1985|title= Weibull Analysis of Reliability Data with Few or No Failures |url= https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00224065.1985.11978953|journal= Journal of Quality Technology|volume= 17|issue= 3|pages= 140–146|doi= 10.1080/00224065.1985.11978953|url-access= subscription}}</ref>
In the late 1960s, Wayne developed a cumulative hazard analysis method for nonparametric estimation of a population's cumulative life distribution. The resulting estimate is most conveniently displayed and interpreted on a probability plot. Until Wayne developed his method practitioners relied on crude approximations for such analyses. Wayne’s paper "Hazard Plotting for Incomplete Failure Data"<ref name="hp"/> in the inaugural issue of the J. of Quality technology received the Brumbaugh Award for the ASQ as the 1969 <ref name="Brumbaugh">{{cite web |url= https://asq.org/about-asq/asq-awards/honors/brumbaugh|title= BRUMBAUGH AWARD WINNERS}}</ref> paper that made a great contribution to the development of industrial applications of quality control. Moreover, his paper "Theory and Applications of Hazard Plotting for Censored Failure Data" was reprinted in the 40th Anniversary issue of Technometrics (2000)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nelson |first1=W. |title=Theory and applications of hazard plotting for censored failure data |url= https://www.jstor.org/stable/1271428|journal=Technometrics |date=2000|volume=42 |issue=1, Special 40th Anniversary|pages=12–25 |doi=10.2307/1271428|jstor=1271428 }}</ref> as one of the "Two Classics in Reliability Theory." Dr. Wayne also developed software that is widely used in reliability analysis; STATPAC is the first complete package for analysis of reliability and accelerated test data, including censored and interval data.  It was the first to provide probability plots, confidence limits, maximum likelihood fitting of many models including accelerated life test models, proper analysis of step-stress data, residuals and their analyses, and a simple user interface.  Its versatile reliability features stimulated imitations in SPLUS, [[SAS (software)|SAS]], [[JMP (statistical software)|JMP]], ReliaSoft, WinSmith, and others.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Meeker |first1=William |last2=Escobar |first2=Luis |date=August 2001 |title=Software for Reliability Data Analysis and Test Planning |url=https://lib.dr.iastate.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1016&context=stat_las_preprints |journal=Iowa State University - Digital Repository |pages=5}}</ref> Also, POWNOR, a software that fits the power-(log)normal distribution to censored life data on specimens of differing sizes.  This was developed on his NSF-NIST-ASA senior research fellowship at NIST to develop better statistical models for electromigration failures of microcircuits.<ref>{{cite report|last1= Nelson|first1= Wayne|last2= Dognanksoy|first2= Necip|date= February 2017|title= A Computer Program POWNOR for Fitting the Power-Normal and -Lognormal Models to Life or Strength Data from Specimens of Various Sizes|url= https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/IR/nistir4760.pdf|volume= NISTIR 4760|publisher= National Bureau of Standards}}</ref>

===Papers===

*'' Residuals and Their Analyses for Accelerated Life Tests With Step and Varying Stress'' Nelson W., IEEE Transactions on Reliability, Volume: 57, Issue: 2, IEEE, 2008
*'' Analysis of repair data'' Nelson W., 1988. Proceedings Annual Reliability and Maintainability Symposium, 1988
*'' Optimum Simple Step-Stress Plans for Accelerated Life Testing'' Nelson W., IEEE Transactions on Reliability, Volume: R-32, Issue: 1, IEEE, 1983
*'' Analysis of Performance-Degradation Data from Accelerated Tests'' Nelson W., IEEE Transactions on Reliability, Volume: R-30, Issue: 2, IEEE, 1981
*'' Prediction Limits for the Last Failure Time of a (Log) Normal Sample from Early Failures'' Nelson W., IEEE Transactions on Reliability, Volume: R-30, Issue: 5, IEEE, 1981
*'' Analysis of Accelerated Life Test Data'', Nelson W., IEEE Transactions on Electrical Insulation, Volume: EI-7, Issue: 1, Pages: 36 - 55, IEEE, March 1972
*'' Hazard Plotting for Incomplete Failure Data'', Nelson W., Quarterly Journal of Methods, Applications, and Related Topics, Volume 1, 1969 - Issue 1, Journal of Quality Technology, Jan 1969

== Awards ==
*Brumbaugh Award of the American Society for Quality (1969)<ref name="Brumbaugh"/>
*Fulbright Award for research and lecturing (in Spanish) on reliability data analysis (2001)<ref>{{cite web |url= https://cies.org/grantee/wayne-nelson|title= Fulbright Scholar Directory}}</ref>
*2003 [[Shewhart Medal]] of American Society for Quality for his technical leadership<ref>{{cite web |url= https://asq.org/about-asq/asq-awards/honors/shewhart|title= SHEWHART MEDALISTS}}</ref>
*Lifetime Achievement Award of the IEEE Reliability Society for outstanding developments of reliability methodology and contributions to reliability education. Nelson was the second person to receive this annual award. (2005)<ref>{{cite magazine |date= Summer 2005|title= WAYNE NELSON Receives Lifetime Achievement Award|url= https://site.ieee.org/schenectady/files/2012/07/2005_Summer_Current_Source_Newsletter.pdf|magazine= Summer_Current_Source_Newsletter|publisher= IEEE}}</ref>
*2010 Shainin Medals of the American Society for Quality<ref>{{cite web |url= https://asq.org/about-asq/asq-awards/honors/shainin|title= SHAININ MEDALISTS}}</ref>
*2018 Hahn Award of the American Statistical Association<ref>{{cite web |url= https://community.amstat.org/qp/scholarshipsawards/geraldjhahnqpachievementaward|title= Gerald J. Hahn Q&P Achievement Award}}</ref>
